chunks.text:
hi bean,

ik i'm super late for this letter, and it's the kind of lateness that's been eating me for weeks. i kept opening the document and closing it. i'd type a line, get up, stand in the kitchen in front of the open fridge until the light clicked off, come back, delete the line. part of me was waiting for the sentence that would be big enough. part of me was afraid that if i wrote too fast i'd put something small on the page when what i have for you is not small at all. both of those are excuses. the truer version is that i made you wait, and waiting is a kind of cold, and you are not supposed to be cold. i'm sorry. i love you. those two sentences belong in the same breath because one is the shape the other takes when i've failed at it.



happy belated birthday.

i love you.

i love you to the moon and back. i know it's a phrase children use; children are just the only people who have not yet been embarrassed out of telling the truth. i love you with an embarrassing amount of attention, with more of myself than i previously knew i had to give. you took my breath away and you keep taking it, over and over, quietly, in the ordinary way, whenever you tilt your head and listen to what i'm saying instead of what i meant to say.

i love doing the small things with you.

because there will always be us, there will always be "text me when you get home", late night that felt endless, dreams whispered in uber rides about a future we couldn't picture all the plans but wanted it anyway. there will always be conversations about epistemological objectivity and ontological subjectivity, about all those promises we'd never lose. there will always be another mason jar that we can collect, a lot more chimpkins that i will cook for you, a lot more laughter towards those curly-waggling shibas, that one day we will own. there will always be another ridiculous wordles or connections that i look forward to every night to solve with you.

you taught me that care has dimensions i hadn't thought to look for. i had filed care under "what you do in emergencies," a kind of response. you are teaching me it's a kind of gardening. steady, daily, mostly unglamorous, attentive to the sort of small changes that only matter if you're looking. i watch the way you look after my skin and apply those small pimple patches. i watch the way you put on moisturizer as well as lip balm for me before bed. i watch the way you tuck the tag back into the collar of my shirt without breaking the sentence you were saying. you have re-calibrated my instrument for noticing. i am so much better at being here because of you.

you are the strongest person i know, and i don't mean it in the hallmark-card register. i mean i've watched you carry things that would have flattened me, and you've carried them without making them anyone else's weight. i've watched you cry and then, after, get up. i've watched you be tired in the bone-deep way where tiredness becomes a kind of weather, and you still asked me about my day with your whole face. i look at you and think, this is what a person who does not collapse looks like.

i want to provide for you, and i mean it in the whole sense. i mean, i want to be the thing you can lean against without having to apologize. i want to be a floor that does not shift under you when the rest of the room is moving. i want, when you are thirty-five, and forty, and seventy-two, for the rituals we have built together (a mason jar in your hand, a shiba asleep somewhere warm, me in the kitchen doing something slow) to still be running.

you made me want to spend my birthday with someone, and helen, you have to understand how strange that is for me. i had always treated my birthday like a deadline, a day to survive with dignity. you made me understand that a birthday is a celebration of the fact that the universe went to four-hundred-trillion-to-one lengths to put you here, on this sidewalk, this morning, with your head full of hope and longing and unfinished business. i want to be on every sidewalk with you. i want to celebrate every absurd coincidence that landed us in the same city with the same stupid luck.

i used to think the private life was just the non-public one, the residual. now i understand it's the only real one. love broadcast is love diluted, and thus what i have with you happens in the kitchen, in the half-sentences, in the specific pitch of your voice when you say my name on a sleepy morning. i don't want to tell anyone about us. i want to keep us in a mason jar on a high shelf that is warm, sealed, and truly ours.

the lateness of this letter matters. i will learn to be on time with the things that matter to you. i will learn to notice the date before it's past. i will learn to write the letter when the feeling is still wet and not wait until it has dried into something more manageable, because you deserve the wet version. you deserve me clumsy and overfull and present.

sometimes, when the dusk settles, and the house finally goes still, when the liveliness of king street has gone down, or that particular slant of light through the glass windows at dawn, how it pooled honey-thick on the floorboards before dissolving into ordinary day, or the weight of unseasonable rain on summer afternoons, or the smell of jasmine tea steeping too long, or standing at the go station watching the train flying by, i catch your eye across the room, and i see her: the same woman who whispered about forever, who cared for me deeply, like a promise that would cost us this much.

i'm living in a dream, because of you in it. not the polished version of the dream i always have, but the tired one. sometimes it's tensions, sometimes it's repair, sometimes it's chaos, and sometimes it's forgiveness. and even now, in the middle of all of this, of all the hardship,...

```sms
    you are still my favorite part.
```

romance looks different with you in it. it looks like a room i'm already standing in. thank you for opening your heart to me. thank you for trusting me with it. i am going to keep earning that trust, on time from now on, letter by letter, day by day, mason jar by mason jar.

i'm still learning how to love you right. sometimes i got it wrong, but you are the one that makes me want to always keep trying, because love is a hill that I will always push towards, because _you_, are the one I want to keep getting better for.

h, i can't wait to do life with you, where we both find ourselves and be there together, for each other.

[^sign]
